Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1231 PM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM FAR
EASTERN IOWA AND NORTHERN ILLINOIS INTO INDIANA AND SOUTHWEST
OHIO...

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EASTERN IOWA
TO THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...AND OVER THE DAKOTAS...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts will be possible
Tuesday from the eastern Iowa/northern Illinois vicinity into parts
of the Ohio Valley and central Appalachians. Areas of severe wind
gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the northern
Plains.

...From eastern IA into IL...IN...OH...Northern KY...WV...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will persist over the region on
Tuesday, while a large area of moisture and instability remain in
place. Several rounds of thunderstorms will be possible throughout
the region, with some uncertainty regarding timing and placement. 
However, the corridor of highest wind damage probability appears to
be tied to early day storms which will be moving across IA. Several
models suggest an organized MCS early on Tuesday, which would then
proceed east/southeast during the day. This scenario seems plausible
as instability will be strong with MUCAPE over 3000 J/kg, steep
midlevel lapse rates, and moderate deep-layer mean wind speeds. A
few significant wind gusts over 75 mph may occur, depending on MCS
organization. Additional late day cells may redevelop along any
trailing outflow, affecting areas from northern KY into WV and
western VA with damaging gusts potential.

...Dakotas into MN and IA...
A surface trough will develop during the afternoon as strong heating
occurs, beneath moderate northwest flow aloft. Storms are expected
to form after 21Z from the Black Hills into western ND, proceeding
east/southeast into the central Dakotas and northern NE through the
evening. Deep-layer shear around 40 kt and substantial instability
will favor cells capable of large hail. 

There is significant uncertainly in whether storms will aggregate
into an MCS, which could potentially spread into more of southern MN
and IA Wednesday morning. If this occurs, damaging winds would be
possible.

..Jewell.. 08/10/2026

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE CENTRAL
HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible
Wednesday afternoon and evening across parts of the central and
northern High Plains. Areas of severe wind gusts will also be
possible over a large area from mid Missouri Valley southeastward
into the Carolinas.

...Northern High Plains...
Modest westerly winds aloft will exist over the central High Plains
on Wednesday, with a surface low developing near the CO/KS border.
Easterly surface winds north of the low across NE will maintain
moisture and instability into the High Plains, and, maximize
directional shear with height. Storms will form over the High Plains
and move eastward through the evening. Hail may occur initially,
with damaging gusts possible during the evening. Capping will become
a concern with eastward extend across NE, but the 40 kt low-level
jet may aid longevity.

...From IA to NC...
Substantial uncertainty exists on Wednesday due to likely areas of
ongoing storms and impacts on daytime redevelopment. That said, the
northwest flow regime aloft will persist across the Midwest and
extending across the Appalachians, with an embedded shortwave trough
moving southeastward toward the OH Valley. This may help focus an
areas of storms across parts of IN/OH/KY. However, areas of early
day storms are also likely across parts of the region, which will
have an impact on severe potential. As such, will maintain a broad
5% Marginal Risk for damaging wind gusts.

..Jewell.. 08/10/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0354 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 131200Z - 181200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Thursday/Day 4 to Saturday/Day 6...
A mid-level ridge is forecast to move eastward through the
north-central U.S. on Thursday and into the Great Lakes region on
Friday. At the surface, a moist axis is forecast to remain in place
from the central Plains east-southeastward into the lower Ohio
Valley. Moderate to strong instability along the moist axis will
make isolated severe thunderstorms possible each afternoon and
evening. Additionally, a severe threat may develop near mid-level
shortwave troughs that are forecast to move through the northern
Plains and Mid-Atlantic on Friday.

On Saturday, a mid-level shortwave trough is forecast to move
through the Great Lakes region. Moderate to strong instability may
be in place over much of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio by afternoon.
Along the northern edge of the stronger instability, isolated severe
thunderstorms will be possible from Lower Michigan eastward into the
central Appalachians Saturday afternoon. Additional severe storms
may develop along an axis of moderate instability over parts of the
central Plains in the afternoon and evening.

Concerning the severe potential from Thursday to Saturday,
considerable variance exists among the model solutions concerning
the position of features, suggesting uncertainty is still too great
to add a threat area.

...Sunday/Day 7 and Monday/Day 8...
From Sunday into Monday, a broad cyclonic flow pattern is forecast
to develop over the northeastern U.S. A cold front is forecast to
move southward across the central and southern Appalachians. This
boundary would be the primary focus for convective development each
afternoon and evening. Ahead of the front, surface dewpoints in the
70s F along with moderate to strong instability would likely support
an isolated severe threat. However, considerable uncertainty exists
concerning the timing of the front. For this reason, predictability
is low at this extended range.

..Broyles.. 08/10/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0753 PM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 110100Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
SOUTH DAKOTA...SOUTHWEST MINNESOTA...AND NORTHWEST IOWA...

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE
NORTHERN/CENTRAL PLAINS TO THE OHIO VALLEY...AND ACROSS PART OF
AZ...

...SUMMARY...
A severe wind swath, with a few 75+ mph gusts is possible across
portions of the northern Plains into the Midwest tonight. A few
severe gusts may also occur over central and southern Arizona.

...South Dakota into Iowa vicinity...

A small cluster of storms near the western ND/SD border may be the
start of what is expected to be a severe MCS through the overnight
hours. These storms are developing within a corridor of strong
instability and favorable deep layer shear. The 00z ABR RAOB shows a
very favorable thermodynamic and kinematic parameter space for
initial supercells growing upscale into a bowing MCS as a low-level
jet increases tonight. This environment is characterized by an
elongated/straight hodograph, steep lapse rates and strong
instability with a layer of drier air around 700 mb atop a very
moist boundary layer. This profile suggests sufficient cold pool
generation is possible, aiding in development of a forward
propagating bowing MCS capable of severe gusts (some 75+ mph)
tonight into early Tuesday. Initial supercells also may pose a risk
for large hail up to 2.5 inches. Reference MCD 1908 for more short
term details.

...Central High Plains...

Scattered strong to severe storms will continue to pose a risk of
damaging winds and hail for a few more hours this evening,
particularly across parts of western NE. With loss of daytime
heating, this activity is expected to gradually wane in intensity.
Reference MCD 1910 for more short term information.

...AZ...

Widely scattered thunderstorms moving westward off higher terrain
will pose a risk for severe wind gusts over the next few hours.

...Northern IL into the Ohio Valley...

Convection ongoing across northern IN will persist into the evening
hours as it track east/southeast into OH. This activity may persist
through the overnight hours moving across much of the Ohio Valley
toward western PA and WV. Damaging winds will remain the primary
hazard, but isolated large hail may also occur. 

...Mid-Atlantic/Northeast...

Strong wind gusts will remain possible with storms along the
southern Mid-Atlantic coast until they push completely offshore over
the next hour. Otherwise, severe potential has largely diminished
along the I-95 corridor and vicinity and severe probabilities have
been trimmed and/or removed. The exception will be across parts of
the northern NY into VT/NH area where a band of strong/severe storms
is ongoing along a surface boundary. Damaging gusts may continue
with this activity for a few more hours. Reference MCD 1909 for more
details.

..Leitman.. 08/11/2026

$$
